# Get-ZbxPassiveProxyLog

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the recent log entries of a running passive proxy session.

## SYNTAX

```
Get-ZbxPassiveProxyLog [-Name] <string> [-Tail <int>] [-Level <LogLevel>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Get-ZbxPassiveProxyLog cmdlet writes the log entries the passive proxy session named in -Name keeps in its own bounded buffer: the connections it accepted or refused, the configurations the server pushed and the data it pulled, with a timestamp, a level and a category. The listener runs in the background, so its log is the place to see why the server does not reach it. -Tail keeps the last entries and -Level the entries at or above a level.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Read the last log entries of a passive proxy

```powershell
Get-ZbxPassiveProxyLog -Name 'dmz-proxy' -Tail 10 | Select-Object Timestamp, Level, Message
```

Each entry has a Timestamp, a Level, a Category and the Message.

### Example 2: Find refused connections

```powershell
Get-ZbxPassiveProxyLog -Name 'dmz-proxy' -Level Warning
```

A peer that -AllowedPeer does not list is refused, and logged as a warning.
